headline: VAR controversy rocks Manchester derby: City win 1-0 despite 10 men
summary: A Haaland goal and Phil Foden's red card spark intense debate over the application of IFAB laws in the 199th Manchester derby.
details: Manchester City secured a 1-0 victory over Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday, despite playing with 10 men for the majority of the match.
The game was defined by two major VAR controversies: a straight red card for Phil Foden and a disputed winning goal by Erling Haaland.
Foden was sent off in the 23rd minute after kicking out at Bruno Fernandes. VAR confirmed the red card, citing a 'secondary movement' that categorized the act as violent conduct under IFAB Law 12.
City's frustration grew as Fernandes, who started the confrontation, escaped punishment, highlighting a recurring criticism of how VAR handles retaliatory actions.
The match's only goal came from Erling Haaland, whose strike was initially flagged for offside but later overturned by VAR.
Semi-automated technology showed Haaland was marginally onside, but debate remains whether Enzo Fernandez interfered with play while in an offside position.
Former United defender Gary Neville criticized the decision, suggesting the offside rule was misapplied and that the goal should not have stood.
The victory allows City to maintain their dominance in the derby, though the officiating decisions have left both sides feeling aggrieved.
caption:
10 men, two VAR controversies, and one Erling Haaland goal. The Manchester derby ends in drama.

Manchester City secured a 1-0 victory over Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday, despite playing with 10 men for the majority of the match.

The game was defined by two major VAR controversies: a straight red card for Phil Foden and a disputed winning goal by Erling Haaland.

Foden was sent off in the 23rd minute after kicking out at Bruno Fernandes. VAR confirmed the red card, citing a 'secondary movement' that categorized the act as violent conduct under IFAB Law 12.

City's frustration grew as Fernandes, who started the confrontation, escaped punishment, highlighting a recurring criticism of how VAR handles retaliatory actions.

The match's only goal came from Erling Haaland, whose strike was initially flagged for offside but later overturned by VAR.

Semi-automated technology showed Haaland was marginally onside, but debate remains whether Enzo Fernandez interfered with play while in an offside position.

Former United defender Gary Neville criticized the decision, suggesting the offside rule was misapplied and that the goal should not have stood.

The victory allows City to maintain their dominance in the derby, though the officiating decisions have left both sides feeling aggrieved.

headline: 8th title: India win Women's Asia Cup by crushing Sri Lanka
summary: India secured their eighth overall title and fourth T20 format win after a dominant 72-run victory over Sri Lanka in Dubai.
details: India defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday to claim their eighth Women's Asia Cup title.
The victory was marked by a record-breaking opening stand of 129 runs between Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana, the highest partnership for any wicket in Women's T20 Asia Cup history.
Shafali Verma smashed 68 off 39 balls, while Smriti Mandhana struck 59 off 39, helping India post a formidable total of 183-5.
In response, Sri Lanka struggled to build momentum and were eventually bundled out for 111, despite India dropping five catches.
The Indian spin attack led the charge with Shree Charani taking 4-20 and Deepti Sharma claiming 3-19.
With this win, India now leads Sri Lanka 6-1 in Asia Cup final meetings.
caption:
A record-breaking opening stand and a lethal spin attack lead India to their 8th Women's Asia Cup title!

India defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday to claim their eighth Women's Asia Cup title.

The victory was marked by a record-breaking opening stand of 129 runs between Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana, the highest partnership for any wicket in Women's T20 Asia Cup history.

Shafali Verma smashed 68 off 39 balls, while Smriti Mandhana struck 59 off 39, helping India post a formidable total of 183-5.

In response, Sri Lanka struggled to build momentum and were eventually bundled out for 111, despite India dropping five catches.

The Indian spin attack led the charge with Shree Charani taking 4-20 and Deepti Sharma claiming 3-19.

With this win, India now leads Sri Lanka 6-1 in Asia Cup final meetings.
